season_context.local_season_notes: Cooler months from November to March are the main season for going out and shopping. Dubai Fashion Week showed SS27 at d3 from 22 to 26 October 2026. Ramadan 2027 is expected to start around 8 February, with Eid al-Fitr around 9 or 10 March, depending on moon sighting. That makes January and February the key buying window for abayas, kaftans and occasionwear.

trends.name: Autumn rich browns and burgundy
trends.summary: UAE autumn edits lean on bordeaux, chocolate and red-brown, deep olive and khaki. Deep purple works as an accent, and menswear favours quieter tonal colour.

trends.name: Barrel legs and pooling trousers
trends.summary: Proportions are exaggerated this autumn. Trousers are barrel-leg or so long they pool on the floor, worn with sharply shaped blazers and fitted jackets.

trends.name: Animal print, plaid and checks
trends.summary: Animal patterns run across clothing, shoes and bags. Plaid, checked shirts and croc-effect textures add character to otherwise relaxed autumn wardrobes in the UAE.

trends.name: Lightweight preppy layering
trends.summary: Practical, light layers suited to the Gulf climate: fine knits, crisp shirts, relaxed jeans and fringe accents, with a single trend piece mixed into an existing wardrobe rather than full looks.

trends.name: Monochrome Gulf couture at DFW SS27
trends.summary: Kuwaiti couturier Yousef AlJasmi debuted a couture line in black, cream and silver at Dubai Fashion Week's October edition, part of a lineup of designers from more than a dozen countries.

trends.name: Corsetry and architectural tailoring
trends.summary: Ukrainian label KEL' showed corset-led, architectural tailoring built around a butterfly motif, and Colombian designer Adriana Capasso showed sculptural shapes at DFW SS27.

trends.name: Multi-craft artisan couture
trends.summary: Pallavi Puri's 50-look DFW debut drew on more than 150 artisans across over 21 traditional crafts, and Tarun Tahiliani mixed Indian handwork with Arab couture codes.

trends.name: Hand-painted gowns
trends.summary: Sara Pedram's Simorgh collection, inspired by the mythical bird, combined hand-painted surfaces with hand embroidery on evening gowns shown at Dubai Fashion Week SS27.

trends.name: Emirati debuts and runway-to-retail
trends.summary: Emirati label Onori by Sharifa AlHashemi joined the official calendar, FAD school graduates showed together, and a buyers' programme plus a Harvey Nichols pop-up sent runway pieces straight into stores.

trends.name: Victorian-inspired Italian luxury
trends.summary: Alberta Ferretti opened Dubai Fashion Week AW26 with a Victorian-themed collection mixing chiffon, leather and tulle, velvet evening capes and feather touches in black, ivory, ruby and aubergine.

trends.name: Kashmiri embroidery in Indian couture
trends.summary: Manish Malhotra closed DFW AW26 with an India-themed couture finale that featured Kashmiri embroidery, Mijwan handcraft and sculpted draping, reflecting the strong South Asian couture presence in Dubai.

trends.name: AI-assisted eveningwear
trends.summary: At DFW AW26, NŪRA by Tryano presented evening pieces developed with AI tools, combining Arabic heritage references with technology. It is an early signal, not yet a retail trend.

trends.name: Coloured abaya dresses
trends.summary: For Ramadan 2026, Gulf celebrities moved beyond black to abaya dresses in red, peach, dark mustard, turquoise and emerald with burgundy, finished with floral embroidery, braided trims or crystals.

trends.name: Abaya over denim
trends.summary: Open, flowing or cape-style abayas paired with straight, flared or wide jeans became a Ramadan street look across the Gulf. Dark denim suits evenings and lighter washes suit daytime.

trends.name: Homegrown made-to-order abayas
trends.summary: Small Emirati labels such as Saintly, Boujee Line and Arod sell playful, statement abayas through Instagram for roughly Dh350 to Dh700, each made to order within about ten days.

trends.name: Luxury-house Ramadan capsules
trends.summary: Valentino, Louis Vuitton, Burberry and Celine released Ramadan capsules of fluid gowns, silk sets, pyjama-style tailoring and embellished bags. Regional labels such as Mauzan and Dima Ayad offered embellished abayas.

trends.name: Sand base with jewel depth
trends.summary: The Ramadan palette started from ivory, cream and sand, then added depth with burgundy, midnight blue and olive, finished with gold, pearl and champagne metallics.

trends.name: Breathable fabrics for iftar
trends.summary: Guidance for UAE iftars favoured linen, cotton, georgette and cupro satin, with silk or satin for a light sheen. Heavier velvet and wool were mostly avoided.

trends.name: Zari and gota detailing
trends.summary: South Asian modest sets worn in the UAE during Ramadan used gold and silver zari, gota strips and hand threadwork, often on chikankari kurtas with palazzos or Anarkali gowns.

trends.name: Eid occasionwear in airy fabrics
trends.summary: Eid 2026 styling for Gulf women paired organza, chiffon, satin and velvet with blush, lavender and mint, or with emerald, deep red and royal blue for evening.

trends.name: Pre-owned luxury for Ramadan
trends.summary: UAE resale platforms promote pre-owned designer kaftans, silk maxis and abayas as an affordable, more sustainable way to build a Ramadan capsule wardrobe.

trends.name: Modest fashion beyond Ramadan
trends.summary: At Shoptalk Abu Dhabi, Chalhoub Group stressed understanding the modest consumer. Commentators urge buyers to stock modest labels year-round instead of only for Ramadan and Eid.

trends.name: Ramadan 2027 lands in February
trends.summary: Ramadan 2027 is expected to begin around 8 February, with Eid al-Fitr around 9 or 10 March, depending on moon sighting. That pulls modest occasionwear buying into January.

trends.name: Florals on coloured abayas
trends.summary: Late 2025 coverage found UAE women choosing abayas in soft blue, lavender, butter yellow and deep red with floral and abstract prints and more tailored cuts. Useful background for 2027 assortments.

trends.name: Heritage-referencing Gulf sneakers
trends.summary: Gulf streetwear grew on youth and music culture. Amongst Few's Reebok Club C collaboration used Arabic-English branding and carpet-inspired interiors, an example of heritage-led streetwear.
